question: The Red Fort was commissioned by which of these emperors?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Red Fort, also known as Lal Qila, was commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638.
 
• Construction of the fort began in 1638 and was completed in 1648.
 
• The fort served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years, until 1857.
 
• It is located in the center of Delhi and houses a number of museums.
 
• The fort's design reflects the peak of Mughal creativity, which combined Persian, Timurid, and Indian architectural styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shah Jahan:**

 
 
• Full name: Shahab-ud-din Muhammad Khurram.
 
• He was the fifth Mughal emperor, ruling from 1628 to 1658.
 
• He is also known for commissioning the Taj Mahal in Agra.
 
• His reign is often considered the golden age of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Characterized by large domes, massive halls, and intricate ornamentation.
 
• Other notable structures include the Jama Masjid, Agra Fort, and the Shalimar Gardens.
 
• It represents a blend of Islamic, Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
 
 
• **Red Fort:**
 
 
• It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
 
• It symbolizes the zenith of Mughal creativity under Shah Jahan.
 
• The fort's walls stretch over 2.41 kilometers (1.5 miles) and vary in height from 18 meters (59 feet) on the river side to 33 meters (108 feet) on the city side.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**
 
 
• India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023.
 
• These include cultural, natural, and mixed sites of importance.
 
• The Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, and Jaipur City are some of the notable examples.
